requirementSpec.intent: Build a polished Roblox main menu titled AURORA. Features: Play, Settings, Credits. Settings opens a panel with Music on/off toggle and Volume slider. Credits opens a small panel. Both panels have Close. Desktop and mobile. Rich glossy cyan/cobalt artwork with thick navy edges, warm gold highlights, ornamental corner details and a title plate. Use Gemini-generated matching skins and icons: button skins, panel skin, slider track and handle, toggle on/off pieces and distinct play/settings/credits/close icons. Keep text live and readable. Create only these features; no shop, rewards, currency, ranks or invented game systems. Play closes the menu and fires a clearly named local hook for game integration. Coherent hover and press animation. Native background layout with restrained decoration. Panels must open and close in the actual controller.

designPlan.artDirection: Premium fantasy-tech menu presentation built around a glossy cyan-to-cobalt material language with thick navy framing and restrained warm gold filigree. The screen stays mostly native and breathable, using a transparent menu dock instead of an outer menu panel so the title plate and three main actions carry the composition. Gemini-generated artwork should form one coherent kit: shared button skins for primary and secondary buttons, one shared modal panel skin, one title plate ornament, one restrained background ornament layer, matching slider track/handle artwork, matching toggle on/off pieces, and a distinct but stylistically unified icon family for play, settings, credits, and close. Live text remains crisp and high-contrast over artwork, with gold used only as highlight trim and not as the main text color. Corners and title plate receive the ornamental emphasis; the rest of the interface stays clean and readable.

composition.focalPoint: The focal point is the vertically stacked main menu dock centered slightly left-of-middle on desktop and centered on mobile, crowned by the AURORA title plate. The Play button is unmistakably dominant through larger scale, brighter primary treatment, and first position in the action stack. Settings and Credits sit directly beneath as a cohesive secondary pair. Modal panels emerge centered over the menu with the Settings panel larger than the Credits panel.
composition.alignmentSystem: Use a strong vertical center axis for title and action stack, with panel internals aligned to a consistent left text edge and right-side utility alignment for close controls. Comparable actions share identical widths within each stack. Ornament placement hugs corners and title framing only, avoiding isolated decorative islands or empty center space.

visualSystem.colorRationale: Cyan drives the primary call-to-action and glossy highlights, cobalt supports secondary controls and panel body gradients, navy supplies the thick structural edge language, and warm gold is reserved for trim, corner ornaments, and title emphasis so it reads premium without reducing text clarity. The dark background and surface tones ensure the live text and bright controls remain readable across desktop and mobile.
visualSystem.outlineStyle: Thick navy outer stroke language with selective inner gold highlight lines on artwork-bearing components. Native text is not heavily outlined; instead use contrast, subtle shadow, and clean panel separation. Button and panel skins should visually imply a 9-slice frame with a sturdy border and glossy top sheen.
visualSystem.shadowStyle: Soft deep navy drop shadow below major controls and modals, with short glossy contact shadows for buttons. Shadows are layered but restrained so the interface feels premium rather than floating excessively.

display.treatment: Used only for the AURORA title over the title plate, uppercase with modest letter spacing and subtle shadow for legibility.

heading.treatment: Panel headings and major labels use clear high-contrast white text with no heavy outline.

button.treatment: Action labels remain live, centered, and slightly condensed by padding rather than tracking; use high contrast with subtle shadow only.

body.treatment: Readable settings and credits body text with generous line height and bright contrast on dark surfaces.

caption.treatment: Auxiliary labels such as value readouts use calm secondary text color with strong clarity.

numeric.treatment: Volume value uses tabular-feeling alignment and bright readability.

badge.treatment: Reserved style role only; not used as a new feature on this screen.

iconSystem.styleDescription: Distinct generated icon family matching the glossy fantasy-tech kit: bold simple silhouettes seated inside the same cyan/cobalt/gold lighting logic, readable at small sizes, with play triangle, gear, scroll/credits mark, and close X designed as peers.

motionSystem.hover: Desktop hover uses a cohesive polish pass: small scale lift, slight upward translation, and a controlled increase in gloss/edge light on actionable buttons. Controls without desktop hover remain still.
motionSystem.press: All actionable controls share a short compression response with shadow tightening and highlight reduction. Toggle and slider handle use the same system but localized to their movable parts.
motionSystem.entrance: On first build, title plate and action stack fade and rise in with a subtle stagger; opening modals uses a quick scale-up from 0.96 to 1.0 plus fade, while the inactive screen beneath remains visible and slightly deemphasized by overlay tint rather than heavy blur.
motionSystem.release: Release returns controls smoothly to resting scale with a brief eased rebound. Closing modals fades and scales them down slightly before hiding.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: If reduced motion is preferred, remove vertical translation, stagger, and rebound. Keep only short opacity changes and minimal scale difference for state feedback.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch devices use Activated and drag interactions only; no synthetic hover. Press feedback occurs immediately on touch begin, and modal transitions stay quick to preserve responsiveness.

audioSystem.touchBehavior: No UI sounds are played on touch or desktop because sounds were not requested.
audioSystem.fallbackBehavior: If a future implementation attempts to resolve audio, it must report unresolved status rather than pretending sounds are satisfied. Current plan intentionally ships silent interaction feedback.

desktop.safeZoneBehavior: Fill the safe area; ornaments stay inset from device cutouts and never intrude on button hit zones.

mobile.arrangement: Single full-screen layered background with reduced decorative density and protected center tap space.
mobile.safeZoneBehavior: Respect notches and rounded corners by pulling ornaments farther inward on top edges.

regions.purpose: Primary title and main menu action stack.

desktop.arrangement: Vertical stack centered slightly left of screen center, title at top, then Play, Settings, Credits with equal widths for secondary buttons and larger Play.
desktop.safeZoneBehavior: Remain fully within central safe area; maintain clear space around buttons for focus and controller readability.
desktop.textScaling: Use UITextSizeConstraint on title and buttons to maintain hierarchy from 1080p down to smaller desktop windows.
desktop.iconScaling: Icons remain fixed peer sizes; button hierarchy is expressed through button size rather than larger icons.

mobile.arrangement: Centered vertical stack occupying upper-middle screen with title plate followed by three full-width buttons for thumb-friendly access.
mobile.safeZoneBehavior: Centered within safe width; preserve top inset from notch and bottom breathing room for modal emergence.
mobile.textScaling: Clamp title and button labels for narrow widths using UITextSizeConstraint.
mobile.iconScaling: Keep icon peer size consistent while button widths expand.

regions.purpose: Centered Settings modal with header, close button, music toggle, and volume slider.

desktop.arrangement: Centered modal overlay with header row, divider, then two evenly spaced settings rows. Music row uses horizontal left-label/right-toggle alignment; volume row gives most width to the slider.
desktop.safeZoneBehavior: Modal stays centered inside safe area with interior padding preventing controls from touching ornate corners.
desktop.textScaling: Heading, body, and numeric text scale independently via UITextSizeConstraint for crisp readability.
desktop.iconScaling: Only close icon present; stays consistent with credits close.

mobile.arrangement: Centered near-full-width modal with vertical content rhythm; header row stays horizontal, rows gain extra height, and volume label may sit above the slider if needed.
mobile.safeZoneBehavior: Respect top and side insets; maintain ample bottom padding for drag comfort on the slider.
mobile.textScaling: Clamp heading and row text to remain readable without wrapping excessively.
mobile.iconScaling: Close icon stays same family and visual weight, slightly smaller relative to button body than desktop.

regions.purpose: Small centered Credits modal with title, body text, and close button.

desktop.arrangement: Compact centered modal overlay with title and close button on top row and short credits body below.
desktop.safeZoneBehavior: Remain centered and smaller than settings modal while preserving legibility and interior padding.
desktop.textScaling: Use heading and body constraints to prevent sparse oversized text in the compact panel.
desktop.iconScaling: Close icon mirrors settings close exactly.

mobile.arrangement: Compact centered modal widened proportionally for readability; title row on top, credits body beneath.
mobile.safeZoneBehavior: Inset from sides and top hardware cutouts; never overlap primary menu buttons when open due to modal layering.
mobile.textScaling: Body text scales down modestly but retains generous line height.
mobile.iconScaling: Close icon mirrors settings close exactly.

regions.purpose: Nonvisual hook and controller objects required for integration and panel behavior.

desktop.arrangement: Logical nonvisual system group under the view root, outside visible layout concerns.
desktop.safeZoneBehavior: Not applicable; nonvisual nodes remain in-root and do not affect visible safe area.

mobile.arrangement: Logical nonvisual system group under the view root, outside visible layout concerns.
mobile.safeZoneBehavior: Not applicable; nonvisual nodes remain in-root and do not affect visible safe area.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: View builds _NexusDesktop containing BackgroundRoot, BackgroundOrnaments, MainMenuDock, SettingsModal, CreditsModal, and system nodes with the exact supported node names. Desktop uses a centered-left dock composition with the modal overlays centered. Play stays clearly dominant by size, not icon inflation.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: View builds _NexusMobile with the same semantic nodeNames beneath the mobile group. When min(viewport.X, viewport.Y)<600, runtime shows mobile group. Mobile recenters the dock, widens buttons, reduces decorative overhang, increases row heights, and keeps all actionable controls at or above 44px touch targets. Settings and Credits modals become wider and slightly taller, while Credits remains smaller than Settings.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Tablet uses the mobile/desktop selection rule but should favor the desktop-like spacing when viewport minimum is 600 or greater. Maintain centered composition with slightly larger safe margins than phone and keep title prominence intact.

implementationNotes: Use the supplied libraryTemplate node names exactly: BackgroundRoot, BackgroundOrnaments, MainMenuDock, TitlePlate, AuroraTitle, PlayButton, SettingsButton, CreditsButton, SettingsModal, SettingsTitle, SettingsSeparator, SettingsCloseButton, MusicRow, MusicLabel, MusicToggle, VolumeRow, VolumeLabel, VolumeSlider, VolumeValue, CreditsModal, CreditsTitle, CreditsBody, CreditsCloseButton, OnPlayRequestedHook, PanelControllerBehavior.
Create _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile root Frames at View.build() return; both trees must exist initially, with desktop visible by default.
MainMenuDock remains transparent; do not add an outer menu panel around the main menu.
Gemini-generated skins/icons are planned artwork only. Do not fabricate asset IDs; resolver supplies assets later.

Use one shared primary/secondary artwork kit: Play gets the primary button skin variant, Settings and Credits share the same secondary button skin, and both close buttons share one compact button skin plus the same close icon family.
SettingsModal and CreditsModal share the same panel skin family; CreditsModal is materially smaller than SettingsModal.
Implement MusicToggle and VolumeSlider as real interactive controls with artwork-derived states/pieces handled inside the existing control nodes; do not add extra user-facing systems.
PanelControllerBehavior should manage mutually exclusive modal state: opening Settings hides Credits, opening Credits hides Settings, and each Close hides only its own panel.
PlayButton activation must close the menu and then invoke the clearly named local hook exposed by OnPlayRequestedHook.
Keep text live for AuroraTitle, button labels, settings labels, numeric volume value, and credits text; do not bake any lettering into images.
Use local helper functions in View for repeated construction patterns, and place runtime button effects in a shared ButtonEffects module rather than duplicating per-button logic.

Use UIListLayout, UIPadding, UITextSizeConstraint, UIScale, UICorner, UIStroke, UIGradient, CanvasGroup, and UIAspectRatioConstraint where appropriate; keep layout constraint-driven rather than position-fragile.
Do not add sounds, shop, rewards, currency, ranks, quests, inventory, tabs, or any extra destinations beyond Play, Settings, and Credits.

The dark background and surface tones ensure the live text and bright controls remain readable across desktop and mobile.
visualSystem.outlineStyle: Thick navy outer stroke language with selective inner gold highlight lines on artwork-bearing components. Native text is not heavily outlined; instead use contrast, subtle shadow, and clean panel separation. Button and panel skins should visually imply a 9-slice frame with a sturdy border and glossy top sheen.
visualSystem.shadowStyle: Soft deep navy drop shadow below major controls and modals, with short glossy contact shadows for buttons. Shadows are layered but restrained so the interface feels premium rather than floating excessively.

display.treatment: Used only for the AURORA title over the title plate, uppercase with modest letter spacing and subtle shadow for legibility.

heading.treatment: Panel headings and major labels use clear high-contrast white text with no heavy outline.

button.treatment: Action labels remain live, centered, and slightly condensed by padding rather than tracking; use high contrast with subtle shadow only.

numeric.treatment: Volume value uses tabular-feeling alignment and bright readability.

badge.treatment: Reserved style role only; not used as a new feature on this screen.

iconSystem.styleDescription: Distinct generated icon family matching the glossy fantasy-tech kit: bold simple silhouettes seated inside the same cyan/cobalt/gold lighting logic, readable at small sizes, with play triangle, gear, scroll/credits mark, and close X designed as peers.

motionSystem.hover: Desktop hover uses a cohesive polish pass: small scale lift, slight upward translation, and a controlled increase in gloss/edge light on actionable buttons. Controls without desktop hover remain still.
motionSystem.press: All actionable controls share a short compression response with shadow tightening and highlight reduction. Toggle and slider handle use the same system but localized to their movable parts.
motionSystem.entrance: On first build, title plate and action stack fade and rise in with a subtle stagger; opening modals uses a quick scale-up from 0.96 to 1.0 plus fade, while the inactive screen beneath remains visible and slightly deemphasized by overlay tint rather than heavy blur.
motionSystem.release: Release returns controls smoothly to resting scale with a brief eased rebound. Closing modals fades and scales them down slightly before hiding.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: If reduced motion is preferred, remove vertical translation, stagger, and rebound. Keep only short opacity changes and minimal scale difference for state feedback.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch devices use Activated and drag interactions only; no synthetic hover. Press feedback occurs immediately on touch begin, and modal transitions stay quick to preserve responsiveness.

audioSystem.touchBehavior: No UI sounds are played on touch or desktop because sounds were not requested.
audioSystem.fallbackBehavior: If a future implementation attempts to resolve audio, it must report unresolved status rather than pretending sounds are satisfied. Current plan intentionally ships silent interaction feedback.

desktop.textScaling: Use UITextSizeConstraint on title and buttons to maintain hierarchy from 1080p down to smaller desktop windows.
desktop.iconScaling: Icons remain fixed peer sizes; button hierarchy is expressed through button size rather than larger icons.

mobile.safeZoneBehavior: Centered within safe width; preserve top inset from notch and bottom breathing room for modal emergence.
mobile.textScaling: Clamp title and button labels for narrow widths using UITextSizeConstraint.
mobile.iconScaling: Keep icon peer size consistent while button widths expand.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: View builds _NexusDesktop containing BackgroundRoot, BackgroundOrnaments, MainMenuDock, SettingsModal, CreditsModal, and system nodes with the exact supported node names. Desktop uses a centered-left dock composition with the modal overlays centered. Play stays clearly dominant by size, not icon inflation.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: View builds _NexusMobile with the same semantic nodeNames beneath the mobile group. When min(viewport.X, viewport.Y)<600, runtime shows mobile group. Mobile recenters the dock, widens buttons, reduces decorative overhang, increases row heights, and keeps all actionable controls at or above 44px touch targets. Settings and Credits modals become wider and slightly taller, while Credits remains smaller than Settings.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Tablet uses the mobile/desktop selection rule but should favor the desktop-like spacing when viewport minimum is 600 or greater. Maintain centered composition with slightly larger safe margins than phone and keep title prominence intact.

implementationNotes: Use the supplied libraryTemplate node names exactly: BackgroundRoot, BackgroundOrnaments, MainMenuDock, TitlePlate, AuroraTitle, PlayButton, SettingsButton, CreditsButton, SettingsModal, SettingsTitle, SettingsSeparator, SettingsCloseButton, MusicRow, MusicLabel, MusicToggle, VolumeRow, VolumeLabel, VolumeSlider, VolumeValue, CreditsModal, CreditsTitle, CreditsBody, CreditsCloseButton, OnPlayRequestedHook, PanelControllerBehavior.
Create _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile root Frames at View.build() return; both trees must exist initially, with desktop visible by default.
MainMenuDock remains transparent; do not add an outer menu panel around the main menu.
Gemini-generated skins/icons are planned artwork only. Do not fabricate asset IDs; resolver supplies assets later.

Use one shared primary/secondary artwork kit: Play gets the primary button skin variant, Settings and Credits share the same secondary button skin, and both close buttons share one compact button skin plus the same close icon family.
SettingsModal and CreditsModal share the same panel skin family; CreditsModal is materially smaller than SettingsModal.
Implement MusicToggle and VolumeSlider as real interactive controls with artwork-derived states/pieces handled inside the existing control nodes; do not add extra user-facing systems.
PanelControllerBehavior should manage mutually exclusive modal state: opening Settings hides Credits, opening Credits hides Settings, and each Close hides only its own panel.
PlayButton activation must close the menu and then invoke the clearly named local hook exposed by OnPlayRequestedHook.
Keep text live for AuroraTitle, button labels, settings labels, numeric volume value, and credits text; do not bake any lettering into images.
Use local helper functions in View for repeated construction patterns, and place runtime button effects in a shared ButtonEffects module rather than duplicating per-button logic.

Use UIListLayout, UIPadding, UITextSizeConstraint, UIScale, UICorner, UIStroke, UIGradient, CanvasGroup, and UIAspectRatioConstraint where appropriate; keep layout constraint-driven rather than position-fragile.
Do not add sounds, shop, rewards, currency, ranks, quests, inventory, tabs, or any extra destinations beyond Play, Settings, and Credits.

changeInstructions: Create a main menu titled AURORA.
Include only Play, Settings, and Credits on the main menu.
Make Settings open a panel containing a Music on/off toggle and Volume slider.
Make Credits open a small panel.
Include Close controls on both panels.
Make Play close the menu and fire a clearly named local hook for game integration.
Ensure panels open and close through the actual controller.
Support desktop and mobile.
Use rich glossy cyan/cobalt artwork with thick navy edges, warm gold highlights, ornamental corner details, and a title plate.
Use Gemini-generated matching skins and distinct icons for requested components.
Use coherent hover and press animation.
Keep the background native with restrained decoration.
Keep text live and readable.
